# Operations ledger

## Shipping labels

Every parcel leaving the dock carries a printed label with the route code,
the weight class and the loading bay. Labels are printed in batches at the
start of each shift, and a supervisor spot-checks one label in twenty
against the manifest. A mislabeled parcel is pulled from the belt, tagged
yellow and set on the sorting table until the next reconciliation pass.
The label printer is serviced on the first Monday of each month, and the
spare roll lives in the cabinet beside the dock door, never in the van.
Torn labels are never taped over; they are reprinted from the manifest.

## Warehouse shifts

The warehouse runs three shifts: early, middle and late. The early shift
opens the dock doors, the middle shift handles inbound pallets and the
late shift closes the building. Shift leads rotate every quarter so that
each lead sees every duty. Breaks are staggered so the belt never stops
for more than five minutes, and the lead on duty carries the radio and the
key ring. Handover notes are written on the board by the door, and the
incoming lead signs below the outgoing lead before anyone leaves.

## Parking and access

Visitor parking is on the north lot, marked with white paint, and
contractors use the east lot behind the fence. Badges are issued at the
front desk and must be visible at all times inside the fence line. The
gate closes at nine in the evening; late arrivals call the desk and wait
in the lot for an escort. Delivery vans reverse into bays two through six
only, and nobody parks across the fire lane even for a minute.

## Holiday schedule

The site is closed on public holidays, with a reduced crew on the days
between them. Shift leads post the rota two weeks ahead on the board by
the door, and swaps are agreed in writing with the duty manager. Overtime
on a holiday is paid at the posted rate, and anyone working alone must
check in by radio on the hour. The canteen serves a cold lunch when it is
closed, and the vending machines are restocked on the last working day.

## Safety walk

A safety walk happens every Thursday morning with a lead from each shift.
The walk covers the dock edge, the belt guards, the extinguishers and the
first aid cabinet, and each finding is written in the safety log with an
owner and a date. Findings that are not closed within a week are raised at
the Friday meeting, and the manager signs the log at the end of the month.
Hard hats are required beyond the yellow line and in the racking aisles.

## Equipment maintenance

Forklifts, pallet jacks and the conveyor motors follow a written service plan.
Each forklift is inspected at the start of a shift, and the operator signs the
checklist before the first lift. Brake pads, mast chains and tyres are measured
against the limits on the card taped inside the cab. A machine that fails an
inspection is tagged red, parked in bay seven and left there until the workshop
clears it. Spare batteries are charged overnight on the east wall, never in an
aisle, and the charger room door stays shut.

## Training and onboarding

New starters spend their first week shadowing a buddy from a different shift.
Day one covers the site map, the radio channels and the fire exits; day two
covers manual handling and the correct way to stack a pallet. Nobody drives a
forklift before passing the written test and a floor assessment with the
training lead. Certificates are renewed every three years, and the training
lead keeps the register in the office beside the canteen, next to the first
aid cabinet and the box of spare badges.

## Waste and recycling

Cardboard, shrink wrap and broken pallets are sorted at the point of use into
the green, grey and brown cages. The yard crew empties the cages every Tuesday
and Friday, and the compactor is cleared on the last working day of the month.
Liquids never go into a skip; any spill is soaked up with the grey granules and
the used granules are bagged for the specialist collection. Wooden pallets in
good order go back to the supplier on the next van that leaves the yard.

## Cold storage

The cold room holds chilled goods between two and six degrees. The door must be
closed within one minute of opening, and the thermometer on the wall is read
and written in the log at the start of every shift. Anyone working inside for
more than ten minutes wears the insulated jacket and gloves from the hook by
the door. Stock is rotated so the oldest cartons leave first, and the duty
manager signs the weekly stock check on the clipboard by the airlock.

## Visitor tours

Tours for schools and local groups run on the second Wednesday of the month at
ten in the morning. A guide from the office walks the group along the marked
path, never across the working floor. Each visitor wears a bright vest and a
badge, and the group stays behind the yellow rope at the dock edge. Photographs
are allowed only from the viewing platform. The tour ends at the canteen, where
the group is given a hot drink and a printed map of the site to take home.

## Incident reporting

Every injury, near miss and damaged load is written on the incident form before
the end of the shift. The lead on duty reviews the form with the people
involved and files it with the safety log. Near misses are read out at the
Friday meeting so that everyone hears what almost happened. Serious incidents
are phoned through to the duty manager at once, whatever the hour, and the area
is closed off until the manager arrives and walks it with the safety officer.

## Reimbursement window

A purchaser who cancels an order receives repayment within nine business
days. The finance desk issues the credit to the original card, and the
confirmation message quotes the order reference.
